It's all a game anyway. You make the $$ so you can give it away.....because you certainly can't take it with ya.

I'm going to voice to text most of this, so if there are typos, I blame software. (Not AI though: I don't need it reading complaints and erasing my bank accounts or something in 5/10/30 years when it takes over the world. I love AI. It will save us all....yeah...we'll go with that.)

I don't disagree with the disparity. It certainly seems outlandish to the nth degree.

However, I'm not quite sure how you stop it.

Reality is even at 1 /1000th this level of net worth, an individual would still have hundreds of times more $$ than most. If not thousands of times more.

In musk's case, as is the case with most high net worth individuals, nearly all of their assets are tied up in a few investments. It's not like any one of them has 200 billion in cash just sitting in an account somewhere.

As an altruist, I do struggle with how to justify this type of net asset acquisition against the rationale that somehow it should be any one of our jobs to dictate what the market will pay for anything.

If doing something illegal, or even immoral, though, I think we can all agree that morality has a subjective definition, often dictated by culture or religion, then I would find fault. Otherwise, who am I to say "VC cannot go out and create 1/5/500 companies that all provide service to the world that the world values at a cumulative sum of $2 trillion. And, as the majority owner of those companies, VC is worth $1T (if he sold all his ownership and the price stayed the same...which it wouldn't)".

In the end, you have to pay the taxman in whatever society you're living based on the laws of that society at the time. It's true, you do not have to give anything away voluntarily. So, in theory, the only benefit to society would be the amount a government takes from you. (Then there are the jobs you have created, taxes along the way, etc, etc)

As a wealthy, selfish person, you're going to choose a government that gives you the most benefits. That government benefits from giving you benefits because some tax revenue to them is better than zero tax revenue too though. So, like business, it becomes a game of who can we entice to move to our municipality/country? How much are we willing to incentivize those individuals/businesses?

Socialism and communism, if looking at it from a pure equal distribution of wealth perspective, will always fail because it's biologically ingrained in all living organisms to seek more. More sunlight for plants. More meat for animals. Sure, there's a symbiotic element to it all, but there's always that one small subset that does not seem to care for the masses, only for themselves. "Prisoners dilemma optimal strategy" be damned!

This is a much deeper conversation than could ever be engaged upon via the forums here. There will be opinions all over the place. Like I said, I struggle internally with both sides. I can argue it from either direction very easily.

The market could stop this type of thing from happening. But it won't, because there's too much money being made by everybody surrounding these companies. Governments could stop this kind of thing from happening, but they never will. First, it would hurt the bottom line of that government to lose such individuals and or businesses. Second, every government on Earth would have to align such that no one government could simply offer a larger benefit and import individuals or businesses. Yet, even if all governments did align, would that have a negative impact on overall human expansion? Sometimes the only thing driving individuals. Is there ambition toward being number one at something.... Not saying that helps humanity as a whole of course.
